title: Decision: authorized-key details (no point check, fragment-only relative references, unique ids)
description:
draft-atwood-mls-didwebvh-credential-00 §Conventions, "Authorized key". Three gaps:

1. "a 32-byte public key in the format of [RFC8032]": must the 32 bytes decode as a valid Ed25519 point? If some members check and others do not, they compute different authorized_keys, so the did_webvh_heads extension differs and members disagree. Chosen: no point check; any 32 bytes count. A leaf with such a key fails MLS signature checks anyway.
2. "A relative reference is resolved against the document's id as [DID-CORE] specifies": DID Core points to RFC 3986 §5.2, under which only a fragment-only reference ("#k1") has an obvious result for a did: base. Chosen: "#frag" resolves to id + "#frag"; an absolute "did:..." reference is used as is; any other relative form ("k1", "?x", "/p") resolves to nothing. Verification method ids are resolved the same way before comparing.
3. Where a reference may resolve to: Chosen: only objects in the document's top-level verificationMethod array (embedded methods in authentication count directly). An id shared by two methods resolves to nothing (DID Core requires unique ids; the document is not made invalid, per the draft's "neither makes the document invalid").

Also: a method's controller must be a string equal to id (DID Core allows a set for the document's controller, not for a method's). crates/mls-didwebvh/src/keys.rs. For -01: say all three.
